literal: Dice and gambling hall and hand (skill), having been infatuated, those who desired eagerly, (are) those who became nothing.
translation: Those who become infatuated with and eagerly cling to the dice, the gambling hall, and the skill of their hands, will become utterly destitute.
modern: சூதாடும் கருவி, சூதாடும் இடம், கைத்திறன் ஆகியவற்றின் மேல் மயக்கம் கொண்டு அவற்றை விடாமல் பற்றிக்கொண்டவர்கள், இறுதியில் ஒன்றுமில்லாதவர்களாக அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
explanation: The couplet warns about the destructive nature of gambling. It lists three elements that gamblers become obsessed with: the dice ('கவறு'), the gambling hall ('கழகம்'), and their own sleight of hand or skill ('கை'). Those who become infatuated ('தருக்கி') and eagerly cling to ('இவறியார்') these things will ultimately lose everything and become destitute ('இல்லாகியார்'). The repetition of the 'உம்' (and) suffix emphasizes how these three elements collectively consume the gambler's life.
